Comparison of DESs with the same HBA but different HBDs DES systems 1 and 3 were chosen to compare system constants and retention characteristics of analytes when the choice of HBA is kept constant but the type of HBD is altered. In DES system 1, TEG possesses ether functional groups that are polar substituents and have the potential to act as additional hydrogen bond acceptor. While 1,8-OD in DES system 3 lacks ether functional groups, the length of the alkyl substituents is kept the same as TEG. Consequently, a comparison of these DES systems truly enables the effect of ether substituents in the HBD to be studied. Slightly higher hydrogen bond basicity was observed for DES system 1 comprised of TEG (Table 2) compared to DES system 3 composed of 1,8-OD as the HBD (Table 3). In contrast, the _l_-term values were generally observed to be smaller for DES system 1 compared to DES system 3, demonstrating higher dispersive-type interactions for DESs comprised of 1,8-OD as the HBD. While _b_-term values were generally zero for DES system 1, strong hydrogen bond acidity of up to (0.48 ± 0.10) was achieved for the [Ch+][Cl−]: 10 (1,8-OD) DES at 60 °C. The retention factors of basic probe molecules (Table 4) provide further evidence of higher hydrogen bond acidity in DES system 3. In addition, DES system 3 generally exhibited lower n-π and π-π interactions compared to DES system 1, as 1,8-OD lacks the lone pair of electrons that are present on ether functional groups in TEG molecules. 3.4. Conclusions Choline chloride and acetate-based DESs are designer solvents that have been extensively employed in separations, organic syn- 9 *N.M. Abbasi, M.Q. Farooq and J.L. Anderson* Journal of Chromatography A 1667 (2022) 462871 thesis, and catalysis due to their versatile and biodegradable na- ture. Since pairing choline chloride as the HBA with a specific polyol as HBD has been known to form multiple eutectic mix- tures each possessing a unique stoichiometric ratio between the HBA and HBD, most studies often screen all possible eutectic com- binations of a DES system to identify the one that possesses the optimal HBA/HBD ratio. While modifying the molar ratio of HBD serves as a useful tool to alter the physical and chemical prop- erties of a DES, its impact on solvation properties has not been fully described using the established solvatochromic dye methods. In contrast, the chromatographic approach employed in this study is capable of thoroughly investigating minor variations in individ- ual solvation interactions of DESs when their HBA/HBD ratio is sys- tematically modified. For the DES systems explored in this study, variations in hydrogen bond basicity and acidity induced by small changes in HBA/HBD ratio were determined to be more drastic compared to dispersive-type and dipolar interactions. Hydrogen bond basicity was generally reduced while hydrogen bond acidity was significantly enhanced when the molar ratio of HBD was increased. Although the decrease in hydrogen bond basicity generally plateaued at higher molar ratios of HBD, hydrogen bond acidity continued to increase up to molar ratios of 1:10. Chromatographic retention of different classes of analytes was significantly altered when systematic changes were made to the HBA/HBD ratio. While acidic probes generally retained the longest on the eutectic mixture comprised of a 1:4 molar ratio, the retention of basic probes was stronger at higher molar ratios of HBD. It was also observed that DESs comprised of [Ch+][Ace−] as the HBA exhibited higher hydrogen bond basicity and dispersion interactions compared to those composed of the [Ch+][Cl−] salt. The presence of ether functional groups in TEG generally lead to DESs possessing higher hydrogen bond basicity and n-π and π-π interactions compared to those composed of 1,8-OD as the HBD. It was also established that TEG and 1,8-OD possessed higher hydrogen bond acidity and dispersion interactions and significantly lower hydrogen bond basicity and dipolarity compared to DESs incorporating them as the HBDs. Additionally, the individual solvation interactions of neat TEG and 1,8-OD were observed to be significantly different, further exemplifying the influence that the choice of HBD can have on DES solvation characteristics. This study highlights the key role played by molar ratios of HBA and HBD in regulating the solvation interactions of choline chloride-based DESs and demonstrates that a suboptimal choice of eutectic mixture in any DES system can adversely impact its effectiveness as an extractant, catalyst or reaction medium, thereby urging the need to design and employ DESs on the basis of their unique solvation properties. ## Declaration of Competing Interest The authors declare no conflicts of interest in this work.
